punchline: In a 2005 review of physicians, more years in practice often went with care that sat further from current evidence.
thirty_sec: Geoff Colvin cites a review of physicians where more years in practice often meant care further from current evidence. His point is that experience does not automatically build competence. Routine practice repeats; deliberate practice targets the hard part with feedback. Later research weakened his larger thesis, but the lesson stands that counting years measures time, not progress.
